title: fix(windows): repair hermes launchers for non-ASCII user profiles with relocatable venvs
claim: ensure_windows_bin_launchers / install.ps1 must not crash (UnicodeEncodeError escaping `except OSError`, leaked .heal.<pid>) when writing the relocatable-venv .cmd delegator under a non-ASCII %LOCALAPPDATA%.

evidence.red: NOT_TESTED: the code the fork patches no longer exists on main, so there is nothing to make RED.
evidence.source: main hermes_cli/_install_repair.py::ensure_windows_bin_launchers no longer writes any .cmd body: it delegates to hermes_cli/_launchers.py (ensure_install_launchers / stage_launcher). The venv-delegator `write_text(..., encoding="ascii")` is gone (git log -S'encoding="ascii"': removed by 3d12e86ef1 'feat(pm): unified package manager — pm store foundation'). _launchers.py now writes .cmd bodies with encoding="utf-8" (L274, L318), so the UnicodeEncodeError crash path no longer exists. install.ps1 no longer writes launcher bodies: it publishes them through `hermes_cli/_launchers.py $binDir` (install.ps1 L995).

upstream_overlap: #122594 (OPEN, liopcc, 2026-09-25) 'fix(windows): keep .cmd launchers and the bootstrap working with non-ASCII user names' owns the remaining defect class on current main: a UTF-8 .cmd body parsed by cmd.exe under the OEM code page, fixed with a %~dp0-relative body, plus the install.ps1 decode fix.
notes: The fork's claim (ASCII write raising UnicodeEncodeError) cannot occur on main. The adjacent residual (UTF-8 bytes vs OEM code page in cmd.exe) is real but owned by #122594. The fork's %LOCALAPPDATA%-expansion idea is a different approach from #122594's %~dp0; at most offer it as a review comment on #122594, not a competing PR. Kanban baggage ignored.
